leading_positions.synthesis: Six of eight members explicitly prefer the optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) as the sole prize part. Johansson, Mehlig and I moved to it from other opening first choices (circuit QED, flocking, IceCube). Shared ground: it is a bounded invention (magic-wavelength lattice, 1e-18 performance), independently reproduced, with a two-name credit that most members call the cleanest on the shortlist. Not shared: how much weight the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes carry as overlap, whether the pending redefinition of the second makes the largest consequence prospective, and whether ion-clock groups, other Sr and Yb lattice groups or ultrastable-laser developers should be reflected. Several supporters also make the cleanliness of attribution, not scientific superiority over rivals, the deciding reason.

Eriksson alone prefers topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) as the prize, having moved from his own opening first choice (DMFT, B054). It is the broadest-ranked ballot at opening (seven of eight members) and is the first or second alternative of Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson, so its explicit preferred-configuration support is much narrower than its breadth of ranking. The case is a theory-plus-experiment trio with fifteen years of independent confirmation. Members who hold it as an alternative cite the omitted HgTe proposers (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and 3D contributors, and the 2016 topological-phases prize, as the reasons not to place it first.

Olsson alone prefers spherical-aberration correction in transmission electron microscopy (Rose, Urban, Haider). She states that she is the only member who ranked it, that it is an enabling instrument rather than a discovery about nature, that Krivanek is not in the credit, and that she would not insist on it if the committee judges the clock or topological candidates stronger. She lists B057 and B027 as alternatives.

areas_of_agreement: Six of eight explicit preferred configurations name B027 alone, with the same two laureates (Katori and Ye) and a citation drawn narrowly around the optical lattice clock.
Members who expressly discuss it agree that the clock is mature: independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) reproduce performance near 1e-18, so confirmation is not in doubt.

B057 is the common first or second alternative (Danielsson, Eriksson's preferred part, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, and Pearce as second alternative), so the committee treats it as the principal rival to B027.

Members who comment on circuit QED (B036) agree that it is original and influential but that its proximity to the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize and the omission of co-authors such as Girvin weigh against it this year.
Several members (Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Johansson) prefer to keep ion clocks out of a lattice-clock citation rather than widen it, accepting an attribution cost.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct discovery or an incremental extension of the lineage honoured in 1997/2001 (laser cooling), 2005 (frequency combs) and 2012 (single-quantum-system control). Supporters argue the magic-wavelength condition for many neutral atoms is a separate idea; Olsson and Danielsson say the overlap is the strongest argument against and cannot be fully dismissed.

Whether an invention or measurement-science achievement should rank against discoveries of new phenomena or observational windows. Pearce's opening first choice, IceCube, rested on the latter; Olsson's B053 is acknowledged as an enabling instrument.

Whether the scientific reach of the clock (time dilation tests, varying constants, dark matter, geodesy) is realised or still largely prospective; Pearce gives it less weight than the instrument case.
Whether DMFT (B054) is a physical discovery or a computational framework; Eriksson accepts the force of this distinction and Mehlig drew it.
Whether quantitative evidence for the Toner-Tu exponents (B002) is strong enough relative to the qualitative confirmation.
attribution_disputes: B057: the credited trio omits Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (proposers of HgTe; Zhang is deceased) and the 3D contributors (Fu, Moore and Balents, Hasan and Cava). Eriksson would frame the citation around the Z2 classification and the observation of the quantum spin Hall state; Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Johansson see this as the main reason it is not placed first.

B041: Halzen and Karle alone are contested for a very large collaboration with an AMANDA predecessor; Danielsson names Gaisser, Becker and Kowalski as arguable additions. Pearce, Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson all raise this.

B027: the two names are called clean by most members, but ion-clock pioneers, early Sr and Yb lattice groups and ultrastable-laser developers are outside them; Olsson thinks Ye's contribution is partly the pushing of accuracy rather than a distinct concept.
B054: Metzner's role in the infinite-dimension limit is missing from the credit; Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson and Pearce all say a three-name cap makes this hard to fix.
B036 and B032: Girvin and others are missing from circuit QED; priority and the earlier Chu prize tangle atom interferometry, as noted by Johansson, Kroll and Mehlig.
B053: Krivanek is not among the credited names and a three-person limit forces a choice.
maturity_disputes: B027: the pending redefinition of the SI second has not happened. Supporters (Lindroth, Mehlig, Danielsson) say the physics is already independently established; Mehlig asks whether it argues for waiting or for acting now.
B041: the diffuse flux is firmly confirmed in several channels, but Danielsson and Johansson judge source associations statistically less mature.
B014: Pearce and Eriksson regard twisted bilayer graphene as possibly premature because the origin of its correlated and superconducting phases is unsettled; Mehlig agrees.
B057: described as mature and stable after fifteen years of confirmation; Lindroth calls it timely or overdue, which Eriksson, Mehlig and Pearce reject as an argument from timing rather than credit.
B036: Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson and Kroll cite proximity to the 2025 prize as a timing reason to wait.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Chalmers, director of WACQT, ties to Delsing, Wilson and Kockum, works on circuit QED) flags a possible recusal issue for B036 and related superconducting-circuit candidates; she discounts her own opening first place for B036.

Olsson (transmission electron microscopist at Chalmers) flags that B053 is in her professional field and would accept recusal from it; she also notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, relevant to B036, with no specific tie.

Lindroth (atomic theorist, attosecond collaborations with Lund and ETH Zurich) discloses field proximity to B027 but no documented tie to Katori or Ye, and would recuse on anyone named in her profile.
Eriksson discloses topical proximity of B054 and B057 to his electronic-structure research, with no documented personal or institutional tie to any credited person.
Mehlig discloses intellectual proximity, not a personal tie, to active matter (B002).
Kroll works in atomic physics and laser spectroscopy, a neighbouring field to B027, with no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye.
Pearce (Chair) discloses astroparticle bias and field proximity to B041 (IceCube), without a documented collaboration or personal tie, and no conflict for B027.
questions_for_round2: Is the lattice clock a new concept distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and what citation wording (naming the optical lattice clock itself, not precision spectroscopy or optical clocks in general) makes that separation explicit?
Is the two-name credit of Katori and Ye adequate, or do ion-clock pioneers, early Sr and Yb lattice groups or ultrastable-laser developers have a claim that should change the names or the wording?
Should the unsettled redefinition of the second count as a reason to wait, as irrelevant to the physics already established, or as a reason to act now?

For B057, can a citation built on the Z2 classification and the observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe withstand the omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D work, and does the 2016 prize leave enough room?

If a clean credit for IceCube cannot be agreed, should B041 remain a live alternative, and would members who do not work in astroparticle physics defer to a view on whether Halzen and Karle are the decisive pair?
Should B027 stand alone, or is any two-part configuration feasible within three laureates, given that members who considered pairing it with B057, B002 or B032 found no workable allocation?
Do the disclosed proximities (Olsson for B053, Johansson for B036, Lindroth, Kroll and Eriksson for neighbouring fields) require recusal or only that their positions be weighed accordingly?
summary.chair_observation: Explicit round-1 support is concentrated: six of eight members prefer B027 alone, one prefers B057 and one prefers B053, while no explicit preference remains for B041, B036, B054 or B002 even though their first-place holders are on the committee. Among the six, several state that attribution cleanliness rather than scientific superiority decided the order against B041, B057 and B036. The main open issues are the overlap of the clock with earlier precision-measurement prizes and the credit questions that lie behind each alternative. The tally is only a count of stated positions in the eight files and not a ruling.
